title: Identification of the global Verdier map with the inverse tensor–Hom comparison
statement:
Use the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions] at any of their four coefficient stages, with admissible structure morphism $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. Use the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the ordinary and exceptional adjunctions [fix-prop-adjunctions], and the projection transformation [def-exchange-projection, fix-prop-projection-formula]. Put
$$C=Ra_!K,\quad \omega=Ra^!\Lambda_s,\quad L=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega),\quad D=Ra_*L,\quad H=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\Lambda_s).$$
Write $\varepsilon_L:La^*D\to L$ and $\mu:Ra_!\omega\to\Lambda_s$ for the ordinary and exceptional counits. For each $T\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$, let $P_T:C\otimes^LT\to Ra_!(K\otimes^LLa^*T)$ be the projection map. Define the specified morphism
$$\alpha_s=\operatorname{curry}\bigl(\mu\circ Ra_!(\operatorname{ev}_{K,\omega}\circ(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L))\circ P_D\bigr):D\to H,$$
where evaluation and currying use the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-adjunctions, lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. Then $\alpha_s$ is the canonical isomorphism of [lem-sf-tensor-hom] at $(f,M,N)=(a,K,\Lambda_s)$, and is also the canonical isomorphism of [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction] at these inputs.

Let $u:\omega_{s,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_s$ denote the canonical identity-adjunction isomorphism supplied by the first assertion of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], put $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_{s,\Lambda})$ and $\rho=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,u):D_sC\to H$. If $e:D_sC\to D$ is the canonical exchange of [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] at $f=a$, then
$$e=\alpha_s^{-1}\circ\rho.$$
Let $F=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], with the tensor and unit comparisons [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor], put $c=FC$ and $c^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c,\Lambda)$, and let $\kappa:FH\to c^\vee$ be the coefficient tensor–Hom transpose of $F(\operatorname{ev}_{C,\Lambda_s})$ through these comparisons. The specified point-dualizing isomorphism $j:F(D_sC)\to c^\vee$ of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex] satisfies
$$j=\kappa\circ F\rho.$$
Let $g:c^\vee\to FD$ denote the canonical global Verdier-duality isomorphism of [thm-pod-global-verdier-duality], transported through the point-fibre identifications. Consequently this map is the specified inverse
$$g=Fe\circ j^{-1}=(\kappa\circ F\alpha_s)^{-1}.$$
At integral coefficients these formulas use the completed operations; at field coefficients they use rationalization and a common finite coefficient stage, respectively. No smooth-purity orientation or Poincare pairing occurs in these map identifications.

source.place: Steps 1–2, at the structure morphism; fix-lem-tensor-adjunction.proof.md Step 1 and lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex.proof.md identify the maps; full verification in report.md

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-structure-hom-chain-realization] to $a,K$ and $N=\Lambda_s,\omega_{s,\Lambda}$. It supplies the finite-Tor domains, identifies the specified counit transpose $\alpha_s$ with both canonical tensor–Hom isomorphisms, and gives $\alpha_sA(u)=\rho\alpha_w$, where $w=\omega_{s,\Lambda}$ and $A(u)=Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Ra^!u)$.

source.place: Step 1, compared term by term with sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom/lem-sf-tensor-hom.proof.md Steps 1–2

proof.text: The identity-adjunction isomorphism $u:w\to\Lambda_s$ is [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]. By [lem-pod-structure-identity-mate] the exchange's structure mate is $Ra^!u$. The construction of [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] is the inverse tensor–Hom map at $N=w$ (whose underlying morphism is $\alpha_w$ by Step 1), followed by $Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,m)$ with $m=Ra^!u$; hence $e=A(u)\alpha_w^{-1}$. Substitution of Step 1 yields $e=\alpha_s^{-1}\rho$. The exceptional adjunction for the identity is supplied by the point lemma.

source.place: Steps 1–2: compute the structure-morphism mate when a_Y is the identity

proof.text: At finite and integral coefficients apply [lem-pod-point-integral-evaluation-normalization] to $C=Ra_!K$, which has the required finite-Tor membership by Step 1. It reconstructs $C$ by the actual sections-extension counit, computes the point-Hom comparison through evaluation (completed integrally), and identifies its specified transpose $\kappa$ and point-dualizing map: $j=\kappa F\rho$, with $\kappa$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Second sentence: explicit Hom-complex comparison and evaluation normalization

proof.text: At $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [lem-pod-point-field-evaluation-normalization] gives the same equation $j=\kappa F\rho$ for this $C$ and proves invertibility of $\kappa$. Its rationalization calculation includes torsion integral representatives and localized morphisms, and its scalar comparison proves independence of the common finite coefficient stage.

source.place: Second sentence at E and algebraically closed coefficients: rationalization and common-stage evaluation calculation

proof.text:
By construction, the canonical global-duality map of [thm-pod-global-verdier-duality] is obtained by applying the point functor to the exchange and identifying its source by $j$; here $F$ is the point functor of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and $j$ the specified identification of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], so $g=F(e)j^{-1}$. Using Steps 2–4 and functoriality,
$$g=F(\alpha_s)^{-1}F(\rho)(\kappa F(\rho))^{-1}=F(\alpha_s)^{-1}\kappa^{-1}=(\kappa F(\alpha_s))^{-1}.$$
These cancellations give both inverse identities. The three coefficient constructions in Steps 1, 3 and 4 use completed integral operations and rational/common-stage passage throughout; no smooth-purity orientation, proper coincidence or Poincare pairing is used.
